title: Evaluation of a strict gate
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $g$ be a gate with at most two inputs, no repeated input vertices, and exactly one input if it is a NOT gate. For Boolean lists $v$ and $v'$, suppose the value of $v$ at index $n+1$ (using false for indices outside the list) is true and its value at index $n+2$ is false. Suppose also that for every input vertex $a$ of $g$, the value of $v$ at the shifted index of $a$ equals the value of $v'$ at index $a$, again using false outside either list. Then the strictification of $g$ evaluated on $v$ has the same value as $g$ evaluated on $v'$.
